title: New Believer
description: The essential narrative arc of the Bible for someone who has never read it: creation, promise, rescue, the life of Jesus, and what his death and resurrection mean — ending in Romans 8, with a closing look ahead to where the whole story is going.
audience: A brand-new Christian or curious first-time reader with no biblical background.

sequence.note: Start where the Bible starts: what the world is, who we are, and what went wrong.
God's answer to the broken world — one family through whom all nations will be blessed.
The God of Abraham reveals his name. 'I AM' will matter enormously when Jesus uses it.
Passover and the sea: the Old Testament's defining rescue, and the lens for understanding the cross.
The rescued people get a covenant. Notice the order — grace first, then command.
Take a breath: the shepherd psalm shows what trusting this God feels like.
And this is what honest failure before him sounds like. You'll need this psalm.
Written centuries before Jesus: the servant pierced for our transgressions.
Now the Gospel written for exactly this journey — 'that you may believe' is its stated purpose (John 20:31).
Cross and resurrection through the eyes of the disciple Jesus loved.
What happened next: the Spirit comes and the church begins.
Paul explains what you just read: why the cross, and what faith is.
The summit, and the end of the road you have been walking: no condemnation, and nothing in all creation can separate you from the love of God in Christ.
Look ahead. Before the new world, the books are opened and God sets everything right. Hope is not the absence of judgment; it rests on it.
And then the last page: no more death, no more tears, God himself with his people. This is where the whole story has been going.
